jobs.occupation: Materialwissenschaftler (m/w/d) (Ingenieur/in - Materialwissenschaften)
jobs.description: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. The work will be performed as part of SPP 2404 DeepDyn with numerous opportunities for collaboration with national and international partners and other doctoral researchers.Development and analysis of numerical geodynamic models that include ULVZsUse of mineral physics modeling tools to compute properties of lower mantle materialsConducting a parameter study with varying ULVZ and lowermost mantle propertiesDevelopment of a probabilistic framework to assess models using seismic observationsAnalysis of the best-fitting simulations in terms of links between ULVZs and plume formation as well as core-mantle boundary heat flux and topographyContribution of relevant software implementations to open-source research softwareCollaboration with international partners who are experts on mineral physics modeling software and seismic observationsPresentation of relevant results at national and international scientific conferences and publication in scientific journalsMaster´s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field (e.g. geophysics, physics, mathematics, planetary sciences or a related field)Fluency written and spoken English languageExperience with numerical modeling or model analysisProgramming experience (preferably C++)Strong background in the dynamics of Earth’s interior, fluid dynamics, or a closely related area (demonstrated through relevant coursework, research experience, or equivalent training)The following are also desirableExperience in the development, analysis and interpretation of geodynamic modelsExperience with the geodynamic modeling software ASPECT or other geodynamic modeling software, ideally including personal contributions to software developmentExperience with quantitative methods for model assessment, statistical inference, or uncertainty quantificationExperience with mineral physics computations (e.g., using...Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.occupation: Informatiker (m/w/d) (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The research group Plankton Imaging Technology and Deep-Sea Zooplankton Ecology at GEOMAR (in cooperation with Kiel University’s Marine Data Science Group) is offering a position in the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” starting at the earliest possible date.The position is offered for a duration of 3 years, with the possibility of extension. In the first year, the successful candidate will be employed by GEOMAR at 75%, supplemented by a 25% contract at Kiel University. Years two and three are fully funded at 100% (pay grade E13 according to the collective agreement for the public sector, TVöD, depending on experience).The position offers the opportunity to pursue a doctoral degree in natural or computer science as a member of the “Helmholtz School for Marine Data Science” (MarDATA). MarDATA’s interdisciplinary focus spans supercomputing, modeling, (bio)informatics, robotics, statistics, and big data methodologies. Doctoral researchers benefit from a structured training program that promotes cross-disciplinary collaboration and provides in-depth scientific insight as well as a systematic approach to marine data science. For more information, visit: https://www.mardata.de/. As part of the MarDATA doctoral network, the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” aims at exploring the use of underwater light field cameras for observing and characterizing plankton organisms (zooplankton) in the ocean. Light field cameras deviate from off-the-shelf cameras in that all rays have to pass through an extra microlens array that changes their direction. Effectively, this means photographing the object from several slightly different perspectives, allowing focussing or 3D reasoning after image capture. The effects intertwine with refraction at the underwater housing and light-medium interaction in front of the camera.The successful applicant willcombine mathematical models for light field cameras and physical principles of refraction and underwater light propagation in order to simulate the image formation processemploy and extend methods of inverse rendering to visually reconstruct plankton from light field imagesdevelop workflows to extract ecological variables from light field imageryinvestigate, how automated classification can be improved by the extra 3D or raw information contained in light field imagesdevelop techniques for geometric co-calibration of light field images with a bioluminescence-sensitive camera in order to create 3D plankton models of bioluminescent deep-sea organismsIt is also expected that the successful applicant will create and contribute to creation and presentation of scientific publications, develop software for calibration, simulation and reconstruction, and is willing to perform and support data acquisition in the lab or at sea during scientific research cruises and collaborate with colleagues from other disciplines as well as the marine technology. Required:Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science or a related fielddocumented successful participation in classes in Computer VisionProfound knowledge in programmingAbility to use Computer Vision and Machine Learning libraries on HPC-machinesvery good English skills (written and spoken)If the university degree has not yet been completed at the time of application, credible evidence must be provided that the degree can be obtained by th...Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.occupation: Life Scientist (m/w/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Junior Research Group Crosstalk (head: Dr. Melanie Mittenbühler) at the Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry focuses on how inter-tissue communication impacts energy balance and metabolic health. We are seeking a talented and highly motivatedPostdoctoral Fellow (PhD/Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 100%) to join our research group. Our group investigates how skeletal muscle acts as an endocrine organ and communicates with other tissues through secreted signaling molecules, particularly myokines. In the ERC Starting Grant project MYOSCAN, we systematically investigate how exercise and age-related muscle loss alter the skeletal muscle secretome. We aim to identify novel exercise-sensitive myokines and define their roles in sarcopenia, metabolic disease, and cancer biology. A central question is whether muscle-derived factors promote or suppress tumor growth and how these signaling pathways can be therapeutically targeted.PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, exercise science, metabolism, cancer biology, or a related fieldStrong expertise in at least one of the following areas: proteomics/mass spectrometry, secretome analysis, cell biology, molecular signaling, metabolic research, or cancer biology. Experience in working with mouse models is preferredScientific curiosity, initiative, strong analytical skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaborativelyExcellent written and spoken English skillsExperience in supervising students or doctoral researchersWe provide a fully funded postdoctoral position within an excellently supported ERC Starting Grant project, an exciting, dynamic and international working environment, and a structured and coherent mentoring and training program. You will be able to learn state-of-the-art methodologies in a team of young scientists. Initially, the position is to be awarded for 2 years starting from 01.03.2027 or later. An extension of the contract period is envisaged. The employment contract is governed by TV-L in its current version for North Rhine-Westphalia, including the special regulations regarding the scientific area. The salary is based on qualification and experience, according to TV-L.Females are especially encouraged to apply, and in the case of equal qualification, handicapped persons will be given preference. The German Diabetes Center is committed to family-friendly working conditions and equal gender policy. Since May 2011, the DDZ is a “Career and Family” audit-acknowledged center. The provisions of § 7 no. 1 of the Act on Part-Time Work and Fixed-Term Employment are taken into account.

jobs.description: Position for a Postdoc (m/f/d) at the Chair of International Political StudiesUniverisity of Witten/HerdeckeWitten/Herdecke University (UW/H) is Germany’s first privately funded university. It was founded in 1982 and has since established itself as a leading educational institution in Germany. Today, the university employs more than 900 staff members, and a total of 3,700 students are enrolled in the Faculties of Health Sciences and of Economics and Social Sciences in Witten.Job descriptionThe team at the Chair of International Political Studies examines the causes and consequences of political violence. Its research focuses on questions regarding the relationship between conflict prevention strategies—such as power-sharing—and the risk of civil war in ethnically divided societies, as well as the impact of local political violence on voter preferences in OECD countries.To strengthen our team, we are seeking a PostDoc (m/f/d) to join the Chair of International Political Studies, starting April 1, 2027. jobs.occupation: Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Ihre AufgabenThe University of Bonn is an international research university offering a broad range of subjects. With a 200-year history, some 31,500 students, more than 6,000 employees and an outstanding reputation in Germany and abroad, the University of Bonn is one of the leading universities in Germany and has been awarded the status of a University of Excellence.The Department of Southeastasia is looking to fill the following position from January 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible, initially on a fixed-term contract according to § 2(1) WissZeitVG until December, 31, 2029Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (65%)Working the Plantationocene. Ecological Labour Regimes of the Palm Oil Value Chain (PALMWORK)PALMWORK examines the relationship between labour and the environment along the palm oil value chain, particularly in the areas of production (plantations and oil mills) and social reproduction. The project is designed as a qualitative comparative analysis of case studies from Northeast India, Ghana and Colombia. It builds on re-search from the fields of labour regime analysis, (feminist) labour geography, environmental labour studies and political ecology on the materiality of nature and the society–nature metabolism. The project is being carried out as part of the DFG Priority Programme 2575 'Sustainability and Resilience of Agri-Food Chains' and consists of three sub-projects located at the University of Bonn, the Free University of Berlin and the University of Kassel. The position is for the sub-project in Northeast India, and is based at Bonn University.Tasks:- Field research with plantation and mill workers in North-East India- Contribution to joint publications- Contribution to science communicationProfile:- A completed academic degree (Master's) in the social sciences or earth sci-ences (political science, human geography, regional studies, sociology or equivalent)- Willingness to conduct independent field research in Northeast India- Very good spoken and written English- Good communication and teamwork skills- Intercultural and diversity competenceDesirable:- Experience of conducting independent research in India- Good knowledge of qualitative research methods- Experience with working and researching with (palm oil) workers- Good command of a language spoken in Northeast India (e.g. Assamese, Bengali, Nepali)- Good knowledge of the project's research area (political ecology, political economy, analysis of labour regimes, environmental labour studies, labour ge ography)What we offer:- Opportunity to pursue a PhD- Be part of a cutting-edge research team- Be part of a larger network of scholars in the DFG Special Programme- Flexible working hours and the ability to work from home- Remuneration in accordance with TV-L pay grade 13The University of Bonn promotes an open, respectful, and non-discriminatory academic culture and is actively committed to equal opportunity and family friendliness. We aim to eliminate structural disadvantages and to strengthen diversity in research, teaching, and administration. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regard-less of ethnic or social background, gender, sexual orientation, religion or belief, disability, or age.Applications from women and people with a documented severe disability (or equivalent status) will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the State Equality Act (LGG) NRW and Social Code (SGB) IXProject start is January 1st, 2027. Please send your application (with motivation letter, CV and writing sample (if available) with the application code 2026/447 to opye@uni-bonn.de. Application deadline is 22th November, 2026.
